candidates.term: The Sage at the Hour Gate
candidates.defline: The Sage stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life you are seen as the one who teaches and protects.
candidates.reading: Because care and knowledge are what you have to give, you pass them on freely, to children or younger relatives or someone you train. Most of your growth in later life comes through teaching, and it sorts out your own thinking as much as anyone's. Your family treats you as the person to call when something goes wrong. You hear other people's troubles far more often than anyone asks after you, and you feel that on quiet evenings.
candidates.teaser: You will end as the elder people consult: knowledge kept warm and given away. Teach deliberately, because your protection of others is what history keeps.

domain_readings.Family: You end as the family’s consulted elder: knowledge kept warm and given away, protection extended to the third generation. Children and students carry your teaching further than your name. Teach deliberately in the last decades. History keeps the shelter you build.
domain_readings.Growth: Late growth gives the learning form: classes, letters, a shelf of notes that outlives you. The last era converts wisdom into artifacts. Make them physical. What you write down becomes the estate that never probates.
domain_readings.Mind: Your mind ages like a library in good hands: cataloged, warm, increasingly visited. Clarity holds because you keep lending it. Stay in circulation always, questions answered, letters returned promptly. The consulted mind is the preserved one.

candidates.life_chapter: Your late chapter is the teaching one: the last decades give away what the earlier ones gathered, and the giving is the glory. Expect to be consulted, quoted, and quietly beloved. Protect the young deliberately, the way someone once protected you. That is the estate.
candidates.relations: The sheltered young are this seat’s people: children, students, and strays who found warmth at your door. They will carry the teaching past your name, which is the better vehicle. Protect them deliberately. Someone once did it for you, and it made everything.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the teaching stays oral: wisdom given, form ungiven. Write the notes this year. The shelf is the succession plan.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the giving empties the giver: everyone sheltered except you. Accept protection from the protected. They have been offering.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, the elder becomes the archive: consulted often, embraced rarely.
candidates.health_line: Your late vitality flows from usefulness and rest in equal measure: teach mornings, nap afternoons, and the constitution carries you far past the tables.

Family.headline: You become the one your family turns to.
Family.recognition: When your family needs advice or a calm word in a bad week, you are the one they call. Because protecting the young matters to you deeply, you step in early when someone younger is struggling, and you give more than you are asked for. You are respected at family gatherings more than you are relaxed at them.
Family.lived: Younger people in your family have brought you their problems since your late forties, and you have taken real care over each one. At least once you have protected someone younger at a cost to yourself, and you would do it again.
Family.ahead: Younger people look to you from your late forties for guidance, and for cover when things fall apart. You give both steadily in these years, and you see what you taught them carry on in their lives.

Growth.headline: You grow in later life by teaching.
Growth.recognition: Passing on what you know is how you grow now, through lessons, letters or the patient answer to a question. Because teaching makes you put your knowledge in order, you understand your own life better each time you explain it. You find a new purpose in being useful to people who are just starting.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties you have found yourself explaining things you once took for granted, and it has taught you as much as it taught others. You have written down or passed on more of what you know than in all the years before.
Growth.ahead: What you know takes a lasting form from your late forties, a course or a set of notes or a body of advice. You see it outlast your own part in it, and you take quiet pride in that.

Mind.headline: Your thinking stays quick because people keep asking.
Mind.recognition: You keep your mind in use by answering questions, reading widely and staying in touch with people who want your view. Because being consulted keeps you alert, you are sharpest in the weeks you are busiest with others. You feel slower in a week when nobody calls, and you pick up the phone yourself before the week is out.
Mind.lived: Other people's questions have kept your mind active since your late forties, the advice asked for and the problems brought to you. You have read more in these years than in your busiest working ones, and you remember most of it.
Mind.ahead: Younger people bring you their hardest questions from your late forties, and you enjoy the work of answering them. You are quoted and asked for in these years, and you feel most yourself when a question has no easy answer.
